claims.text: James Carlson, son of Echo Flight crew commander Capt. Eric D. Carlson, has published a 357-page work titled 'American, Credulous' and a shorter piece titled 'Echo Flights of Fantasy - Anatomy of a UFO Hoax', concluding that no UFOs were involved at Echo Flight or any other flight and that claims of UFO interference are completely unsupportable.

His enumerated disputes with Robert Salas are: that Salas claims all ten Echo Flight missiles shut down where Eric Carlson confirms three or four; that no Oscar Flight incident occurred on 24 or 25 March 1967; that Walt Figel denied seeing a UFO; that Salas has located himself inconsistently across accounts; and that Salas never witnessed anything directly, his account being of a telephone call from a topside security policeman.

One of his disputes is settled against him by the Air Force's own paper. The 341st SMW history states that all launch facilities in Echo Flight lost strategic alert nearly simultaneously, which supports Salas's figure of ten and not the three-or-four figure Carlson attributes to his father.

claims.source: 341st SMW history, Jan-Mar 1967, p 38, and a full-text search of the 88-page release, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: One of his disputes is supported by the same document. The words 'Unidentified Flying Object' occur exactly once in the 88 released pages of the 341st SMW histories, and the occurrence is a negative: 'Rumors of Unidentified Flying Objects (UFO) around the area of Echo Flight during the time of fault were disproven.' The string 'Oscar' does not occur in the release at all.

conflicts: The board's own reading of the primary document splits his case in two: the unit history contradicts his father's three-or-four figure and supports Salas, while the same history's single UFO sentence and its silence on Oscar Flight support Carlson. Neither side's account of this document survives intact.

label: James Carlson
narrative: James Carlson is the principal named opponent of the Malmstrom UFO account and the son of the officer who commanded Echo Flight on 16 March 1967. He has published a long work, 'American, Credulous', reported at 357 pages, and a shorter piece, 'Echo Flights of Fantasy - Anatomy of a UFO Hoax', in which he argues that no UFOs were involved at Echo Flight or any other Malmstrom flight and that the claim of UFO interference with the missile force is unsupportable. His disputes with Robert Salas are specific and enumerable rather than rhetorical: the number of missiles affected, whether an Oscar Flight incident occurred at all, what Walter Figel actually said, which flight Salas was assigned to, and the fact that Salas did not himself witness anything. He belongs on this board under CLAUDE.md section 2a on notability: an informed reader looking at the Malmstrom cluster would expect to find the case against inside it, and the triage rule requires the case against to live on the same nodes rather than in a separate file. The board records his position and does not adopt it. Note the symmetry the cluster produces: his father's denial reaches the public through him, exactly as Figel's admission reaches the public through Robert Hastings.
